content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Employee: Terri Koch (E009), requests admin access to Payroll.

Note 1 says: role Engineer, employment type full_time, recommendation for Payroll: write. Comment says she's a full-time Engineer, requested admin on Payroll, but her role does not own Payroll, so admin is not allowed. Maximum is write.

Note 2 says: role Engineer, employment type contractor, security training basic, recommendation for Payroll: read. Comment says contractor, basic security training, requested admin on Payroll. Contractors can never have admin; write requires advanced training. Maximum is read.

There's a conflict between the two notes: one says full_time, one says contractor. As the Approver, I need to decide based on the info available. The two notes contradict each other on employment type and maximum.

Hmm. The facts are conflicting. I need to make a decision. Let me think about what the right call is.

The requested level is admin. Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role. Terri is an Engineer. Neither note allows admin: full-time Engineer doesn't own Payroll, so max is write. Contractor can never be admin, max is read (basic training).

So admin is above the maximum in both interpretations. Never grant more than requested; grant the maximum. But which maximum - write or read?

The two notes conflict. As the approver, I should probably be conservative? The policy says maximum based on employment type. One note says full_time (max write), other says contractor (max read). The safer/secure choice given conflicting info would be read. But actually, let me consider: which note is more authoritative? Both are from HR/Security agents. Note 1 appears to be from HR (employment facts), note 2 from Security? Actually both notes are labeled ticket 1.

Given conflicting facts, the conservative security-minded approach is to grant the lower maximum (read). Also, both recommendations: write vs read. The safest is read.

I'll grant read, since the contractor classification with basic training limits to read, and granting the minimum of conflicting maxima is the safe choice. The requester wanted admin; grant maximum allowed under the more restrictive reading = read.

Let me submit decision: read.
